name: Gerdy-tubercle osteotomy approach for a lateral Hoffa fracture
region: lateral knee and posterior lateral femoral condyle
corridor: Extended lateral knee exposure with osteotomy of the iliotibial-band insertion at Gerdy tubercle to reach the posterior lateral condyle

positioning.text: Position supine with a bump or lateral tilt and the knee freely flexible so the lateral and posterior condyle can be accessed and imaged.

setup.text: Review thin-cut CT for fragment morphology, plan osteotomy fixation before incision, and prepare direct posterior-condyle reduction, lag-screw, and buttress options.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark patella, joint line, fibular head, Gerdy tubercle, iliotibial band, lateral epicondyle, and peroneal-nerve course.

incision.text: Use a lateral knee incision centered over the distal iliotibial band and Gerdy tubercle, extending proximally and distally for the planned osteotomy and condylar access.

superficial_interval.text: Expose the iliotibial-band insertion as a repairable unit, preserve lateral sensory tissue, and identify the posterolateral danger zone before osteotomy.

deep_interval.text: Create and mobilize a controlled Gerdy-tubercle osteotomy with the iliotibial-band attachment, then develop the lateral capsular interval to the posterior lateral femoral condyle.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band and Gerdy insertion, osteotomy fragment, lateral capsule and posterolateral soft tissues, then posterior lateral condyle.

structures_encountered.text: Iliotibial band, Gerdy tubercle, lateral capsule, lateral meniscus, lateral collateral and popliteus region, posterior condylar cartilage, and Hoffa fragment are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Common peroneal nerve, popliteal vessels, lateral meniscus, popliteus, lateral collateral complex, articular cartilage, and osteotomy fragment are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Posterior dissection and posterior-to-anterior drilling approach the popliteal bundle; maintain direct bony contact, guarded depth, and fluoroscopic control.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid forceful posterolateral retraction that tensions the peroneal nerve or collateral structures, and protect the meniscus and cartilage from retractors.

exposure.text: Provides direct access to the posterior lateral condylar articular surface and enables posterior-to-anterior lag-screw placement or posterior buttressing.

limitations.text: This specialized approach adds an osteotomy requiring repair and is not appropriate for medial Hoffa fragments or fractures adequately exposed by a standard parapatellar route.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along the lateral distal femur or combine with a parapatellar arthrotomy when broader anterior articular visualization is required.

indications.text: Use selectively for a lateral coronal-plane Hoffa fracture when posterior fragment visualization and posterior-to-anterior fixation cannot be achieved safely through a simpler exposure.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid for medial condylar fragments, inadequate Gerdy-tubercle bone, compromised lateral soft tissue, or when an alternative approach provides equivalent access without osteotomy.

implant_implications.text: Plan posterior-to-anterior lag screws perpendicular to the fracture, add a buttress when shear demands it, and securely refix the Gerdy osteotomy without joint penetration.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, oblique, and tangential condylar views to confirm articular reduction, posterior screw start and length, and osteotomy fixation.

closure.text: Repair the capsule and any released lateral structures, anatomically reduce and fix the Gerdy fragment with the iliotibial band tension restored, then close fascia and skin.

complications.text: Complications include peroneal or popliteal injury, osteotomy nonunion or displacement, articular malreduction, stiffness, ligament or meniscal injury, infection, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: If posterior visualization remains unsafe, add a complementary exposure or revise fixation direction rather than drilling blindly toward the popliteal fossa.

procedure_applications.condition: A lateral Hoffa fragment requires posterior articular access and posterior-to-anterior lag-screw or buttress fixation

questions.question: What fracture is the classic indication?
questions.answer: A lateral femoral-condyle Hoffa fracture needing posterior fixation.

questions.question: What structure remains attached to the osteotomy fragment?
questions.answer: The iliotibial band at Gerdy tubercle.

questions.question: Why use posterior-to-anterior screws?
questions.answer: They can be placed perpendicular to the coronal fracture plane and provide compression.
